keyword: when will artemis get to the moon

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a crewed mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: NASA's Artemis II astronauts (R1); four astronauts (R2, R3, R4, R5, R7, R8, R9); crew of four (R6)
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly describe Artemis II as carrying a crew of four astronauts.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT [April 1, 2026] (R1); launched on Wednesday evening [April 1, 2026] (R2); launched on 1 April 2026 (R3, R4, R5, R7, R8, R9)
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm the exact launch date and time as April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to reach the neighborhood of the moon around April 6, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: roughly a four-day journey to the far side of the moon [from April 1 launch] (R1); day six of the mission—Monday, April 6 (R4); sixth day of the mission (R6); Day six (6 April) (R7); lunar flyby on April 6 (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references specify arrival at the moon on the sixth day, aligning with April 6 from an April 1 launch.

verifications.claim: Artemis II reaches the neighborhood of the moon on its sixth day.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: day six of the mission (R4); sixth day of the mission (R6); Day six (6 April) (R7); lunar flyby today [day 6] (R9)
verifications.reasoning: References directly state the moon approach/flyby occurs on the sixth day of the mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II passes within 4,000 miles of the moon's surface without landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit. Instead, the plan is to loop around it (R1); fly within about 4,000 miles above the surface (R2); as close as 4,000 miles (R4); at least 4,000 nautical miles above (R6); 4,600 miles (R7); closest approach to the Moon at about 6,545 kilometers (4,067 miles) (R9)
verifications.reasoning: References confirm no landing/orbit and closest approach around 4,000 miles (4,067-4,600 miles consistently cited).

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a crewed flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: loop around [the moon] (R1); around the moon but not land there (R2); journey around the moon (R3); whip around the lunar far side (R4); lunar flyby mission (R5); one pass around the moon (R6); swing around the far side (R7, R9)
verifications.reasoning: All describe it as a crewed mission looping/flying by/passing around the moon without landing.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: From launch ... to splashdown on April 10, the mission is slated to last about nine and a half days (R1); 10-day mission (R2, R3, R4, R5, R7, R8, R9)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as a 10-day (or ~9.5-10 day) mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a test flight to check systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: thoroughly test their Orion capsule (R1); check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey (R2); shakedown mission test-flying the Orion spacecraft (R4); test flight (R5); test of the technology (R7); test flight (R8); test Orion’s systems (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly called a test flight to verify spacecraft systems.

verifications.claim: Artemis II orbits the far side of the moon before returning to Earth.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit. Instead, the plan is to loop around it (R1); not entering low lunar orbit (R2); whip around the lunar far side (R4); flyby (R5); make one pass around the moon, never entering low-lunar orbit (R6); swing around the far side (R7); pass around the Moon (R9)
verifications.reasoning: References specify no lunar orbit; it's a flyby/loop/pass around the far side, not an orbit.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first human trip to the moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago [1972] (R1); first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years (R3); since Apollo 17 in 1972 (R4, R5, R6); first humans back to the Moon in over 50 years (R9)
verifications.reasoning: All confirm first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is a moon landing test.
verifications.label: INCORRECT

verifications.reasoning: References describe Artemis III as docking/lander test in Earth orbit, not a moon landing.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is planned for mid-2027.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Artemis III in mid-2027 (R5); Artemis 3 ... mid-2027 (R7); Artemis III, in 2027 (R8)
